# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

@startuml

class Alive {

    toUnicodeChar() : char

    minePosition : Position
}

    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char

    toUnicodeChar() : char

    getNumGems() : int
    getRow(row : int) : List<Cell>

}

During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pesudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.
2. For each operation specification, determine whether it is complete and consistent with the requirement.
3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getRow
Summary: Retrieves all cells belonging to a specific row.
Algorithm: return board[row];
Related Features: board
Related Classes: Cell
Input: row (int): Target row index. Range: 0 <= row < numRows.
Output: List<Cell>: List of cells in the specified row.
Pre-condition: row is within valid board bounds.
Post-condition: Returns the list of cells for the given row.

GameBoard::getCol
Summary: Retrieves all cells belonging to a specific column.
Algorithm:
Related Features: board, numRows
Related Classes: Cell
Input: col (int): Target column index. Range: 0 <= col < numCols.
Output: List<Cell>: Ordered list of cells in the column (top to bottom).
Pre-condition: col is within valid board bounds.
Post-condition: Returns a list containing all cells in the specified column.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary: Retrieves the cell at the specified Position object.
Algorithm: return getCell1(position.row, position.col);
Related Features: position.row, position.col
Related Classes: Position, Cell
Input: position (Position): Encapsulated grid coordinates.
Output: Cell: The cell object at the given position.
Pre-condition: position.row and position.col are within valid board bounds.
Post-condition: Returns the Cell instance at position.

GameBoard::getEntityCell1
Summary: Retrieves the EntityCell at the specified Position.
Algorithm: Cell c = getCell2(position); return (EntityCell) c;
Related Features: getCell2
Related Classes: Position, EntityCell, Cell
Input: position (Position): Target location.
Output: EntityCell: The entity-containing cell at the position.
Pre-condition: position is valid and points to a cell that is an instance of EntityCell.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
MoveStack::peek
Summary: Returns the most recent move without removing it.
Algorithm: return this.moves.get(this.moves.size() - 1);
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: None.
Output: MoveResult: Top element.
Pre-condition: Stack is not empty.
Post-condition: Returns top move. Stack unchanged.

MoveStack::push
Summary: Records a move result onto the undo stack.
Algorithm: this.moves.add(move);
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: move (MoveResult): Move to record. Range: Non-null.
Output: void
Pre-condition: move is not null.
Post-condition: Move added to stack top.

MoveStack::isEmpty
Summary: Checks if the undo stack contains any moves.
Algorithm: return this.moves.isEmpty();
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: boolean: true if empty.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
MoveStack::peek
Summary: Returns the most recent move without removing it.
Algorithm: return this.moves.get(this.moves.size() - 1);
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: None.
Output: MoveResult: Top element.
Pre-condition: Stack is not empty.
Post-condition: Returns top move. Stack unchanged.

MoveStack::push
Summary: Records a move result onto the undo stack.
Algorithm: this.moves.add(move);
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: move (MoveResult): Move to record. Range: Non-null.
Output: void
Pre-condition: move is not null.
Post-condition: Move added to stack top.

MoveStack::isEmpty
Summary: Checks if the undo stack contains any moves.
Algorithm: return this.moves.isEmpty();
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: None
Input: None.
Output: boolean: true if empty.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns stack emptiness status.

MoveStack::pop
Summary: Removes and returns the top move, recording the undo action.
Algorithm:
Related Features: moves, popCount
Related Classes: MoveResult
Input: None.
Output: MoveResult: Removed move.
Pre-condition: Stack is not empty.
Post-condition: Top move removed, popCount incremented.

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pesudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.
2. For each operation specification, determine whether it is complete and consistent with the requirement.
3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameController::processMove
Summary: Orchestrates move execution, state counters, life management, and move stack persistence.
Algorithm: result = gameBoardController.makeMove(direction); if result instanceof Invalid: return result; if result instanceof Alive: gameState.incrementNumMoves(); if result.collectedExtraLives.size > 0: gameState.increaseNumLives(result.collectedExtraLives.size()); gameState.moveStack.push(result); if result instanceof Dead: gameState.incrementNumMoves(); gameState.incrementNumDeaths(); gameState.decrementNumLives(); return result;
Related Features: gameBoardController, gameState.numMoves, gameState.numDeaths, gameState.numLives, gameState.moveStack, hasUnlimitedLives
Related Classes: GameBoardController, GameState, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, MoveStack
Input: direction (Direction): Movement direction.
Output: MoveResult: Outcome of the move.
Pre-condition: Game is active.
Post-condition: State counters updated appropriately. Stack updated only for Alive. Lives adjusted. Returns result.

GameController::processUndo
Summary: Undoes the last valid move, restores state, and manages undo tracking.
Algorithm: if gameState.moveStack.isEmpty(): return false; prevMove = gameState.moveStack.pop(); gameState.gameBoardController.undoMove(prevMove); gameState.decreaseNumLives(prevMove.collectedExtraLives.size()); return true;
Related Features: gameState.moveStack, gameState.gameBoardController, gameState.numLives, alive.collectedExtraLives
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoardController, MoveStack, MoveResult, Alive
Input: None.
Output: boolean: true if undo successful, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: At least one Alive move in stack.
Post-condition: Last Alive move reverted. Extra lives decreased. Stack popped. numMoves unchanged. popCount incremented. Returns true.

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getRow
Summary: Returns a list of all cells in a specific row.
Algorithm: list = new List<Cell>(); for c from 0 to numCols-1: list.add(board[row][c]); return list;
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: Cell
Input: row (int): Row index.
Output: List<Cell>: Cells in that row.
Pre-condition: 0 <= row < numRows.
Post-condition: Returns a new list containing references to cells in the specified row. Board unchanged.

GameBoard::getCol
Summary: Returns a list of all cells in a specific column.
Algorithm: list = new List<Cell>(); for r from 0 to numRows-1: list.add(board[r][col]); return list;
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: Cell
Input: col (int): Column index.
Output: List<Cell>: Cells in that column.
Pre-condition: 0 <= col < numCols.
Post-condition: Returns a new list containing references to cells in the specified column. Board unchanged.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary: Retrieves the cell at the specified Position object.
Algorithm: pos = position; return getCell1(pos.row, pos.col);
Related Features: getCell1
Related Classes: Position, Cell
Input: position (Position): Grid coordinate.
Output: Cell: The cell at the position.
Pre-condition: position.row and position.col are within board bounds.
Post-condition: Returns the cell corresponding to the extracted coordinates.

Related Features: getEntityCell1

Output: EntityCell: The entity cell.

GameBoard::getCell1

Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: Cell

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getRow
Summary: Returns a list of all cells in a specific row.
Algorithm: list = new List<Cell>(); for c from 0 to numCols-1: list.add(board.get(row, c)); return list;
Related Features: board, numCols
Related Classes: Cell
Input: row (int): Row index.
Output: List<Cell>: Cells in that row.
Pre-condition: 0 <= row < numRows.
Post-condition: Returns a new list containing references to cells in the specified row. Board unchanged.

GameBoard::getCol
Summary: Returns a list of all cells in a specific column.
Algorithm: list = new List<Cell>(); for r from 0 to numRows-1: list.add(board.get(r, col)); return list;
Related Features: board, numRows
Related Classes: Cell
Input: col (int): Column index.
Output: List<Cell>: Cells in that column.
Pre-condition: 0 <= col < numCols.
Post-condition: Returns a new list containing references to cells in the specified column. Board unchanged.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary: Retrieves the cell at the specified Position object.
Algorithm: return getCell1(position.row, position.col);
Related Features: getCell1
Related Classes: Position, Cell
Input: position (Position): Grid coordinate.
Output: Cell: The cell at the position.
Pre-condition: position.row and position.col are within board bounds.
Post-condition: Returns the cell corresponding to the extracted coordinates.

GameBoard::getEntityCell1
Summary: Gets the EntityCell at a given Position.
Algorithm: cell = getCell2(position); return (EntityCell) cell;
Related Features: getCell2
Related Classes: EntityCell, Position, Cell
Input: position (Position): Target location.
Output: EntityCell: The entity cell at the location.
Pre-condition: Position is valid and the cell at that position is an EntityCell.
Post-condition: Returns the EntityCell reference. No state changes.

GameBoard::getEntityCell2
Summary: Gets the EntityCell at given row and column indices.
Algorithm: pos = new Position(row, col); return getEntityCell1(pos);
Related Features: getEntityCell1
Related Classes: EntityCell, Position
Input: row (int), col (int): Coordinates.
Output: EntityCell: The entity cell.
Pre-condition: Valid bounds, cell is an EntityCell.
Post-condition: Returns the EntityCell. No state changes.

GameBoard::getCell1
Summary: Retrieves the cell at the specified row and column indices.
Algorithm: if 0 <= row < numRows and 0 <= col < numCols: return board.get(row, col); else: throw IndexOutOfBoundsException;
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: Cell
Input: row (int), col (int): Grid coordinates.
Output: Cell: The cell object at the given coordinates.
Pre-condition: 0 <= row < numRows and 0 <= col < numCols.
Post-condition: Returns the exact cell instance stored at the given coordinates. No state changes.

GameBoard::getNumGems
Summary: Counts and returns the number of Gems currently present on the GameBoard (remaining Gems).
Algorithm: count = 0; for r from 0 to numRows-1: for c from 0 to numCols-1: cell = getCell1(r, c); if cell instanceof Gem: count++; return count;
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: Gem, Cell
Input: None.
Output: int: Number of remaining gems.
Pre-condition: Board is initialized.
Post-condition: Returns accurate count of Gem instances. No side effects. Aligns with GameState win condition (getNumGems() == 0).

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Entity::setowner
Summary: Assigns the owner cell to this entity and establishes bidirectional linkage with the cell.
Algorithm: this.owner = owner; owner.setentity(this); return owner;
Related Features: owner
Related Classes: EntityCell
Input: owner (EntityCell): The cell that will contain this entity.
Output: EntityCell: The newly assigned owner cell.
Pre-condition: owner is not null.
Post-condition: this.owner equals owner, and owner.entity equals this.

the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

Entity::setowner

Related Features: owner
Related Classes: EntityCell
Input: owner (EntityCell): The cell that will contain this entity.
Output: EntityCell: The newly assigned owner cell.
Pre-condition: owner is not null.
Post-condition: this.owner equals owner, and owner.entity equals this.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

Position::offsetByOrNull1
Summary: Computes offset and returns null if the result falls outside the board boundaries.
Algorithm: nr = row + dRow; nc = col + dCol; if 0 <= nr < numRows and 0 <= nc < numCols: return new Position(nr, nc); else: return null;
Related Features: row, col
Related Classes: Position

You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pesudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.
2. For each operation specification, determine whether it is complete and consistent with the requirement.
3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

Post-condition: numLives decreased by 1 unless unlimited. Returns updated value.

GameState::getScore

Algorithm: collected = initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(); undoes = moveStack.popCount; initialBoardSize = initialNumRows * initialNumCols; // inferred from board dimensions score = initialBoardSize + (collected * 10) - (numMoves * 1) - (undoes * 2) - (numDeaths * 4); return score;
Related Features: initialNumOfGems, gameBoard, moveStack.popCount, numMoves, numDeaths, getNumGems()
Related Classes: GameBoard, MoveStack
Input: None.
Output: int: Calculated score.
Pre-condition: Game state initialized.
Post-condition: Returns computed score according to formula. No state change.

GameState::decreaseNumLives
Summary: Decreases the life count by a specified delta, respecting unlimited lives mode.

Related Features: numLives, hasUnlimitedLives
Related Classes: None
Input: delta (int): Amount to decrease.
Output: int: Updated life count.
Pre-condition: delta >= 0.
Post-condition: numLives reduced by delta unless in unlimited mode. Returns updated value.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoardController::makeMove
Summary: Executes inertial sliding logic for a given direction, determining movement outcome and handling collections/deaths.
Algorithm: curr = gameBoard.player.position; dirDelta = Direction.toOffset(direction); dist = 0; while true: nextPos = curr.offsetByOrNull1(dirDelta.dRow, dirDelta.dCol, numRows, numCols); if nextPos == null or gameBoard.getCell(nextPos) instanceof Wall: break; curr = nextPos; dist++; cell = gameBoard.getCell(curr); if cell instanceof StopCell: break; if cell instanceof Mine: return new Dead(gameBoard.player.position, curr); if cell instanceof Gem or ExtraLife: record collection; continue; if dist == 0: return new Invalid(); remove collected items from board; update gameBoard.player.position = curr; return new Alive(gameBoard.player.position, curr, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
Related Features: gameBoard.player, gameBoard.getCell, Direction deltas, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Gem, Mine, StopCell, ExtraLife
Related Classes: GameBoard, Direction, Position, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Gem, Mine, StopCell, ExtraLife
Input: direction (Direction): UP, DOWN, LEFT, or RIGHT.
Output: MoveResult: Alive, Dead, or Invalid.
Pre-condition: Player is on board. Board configuration is complete.
Post-condition: Board updated (gems/lives removed if Alive). Player position updated only if Alive. Returns appropriate result type.

GameBoardController::undoMove
Summary: Reverses a previous Alive move on the board, restoring positions and collected items.
Algorithm: if prevMove not instanceof Alive: throw IllegalArgumentException; alive = (Alive) prevMove; gameBoard.player.position = alive.origPosition; for gemPos in alive.collectedGems: place Gem at gemPos; for lifePos in alive.collectedExtraLives: place ExtraLife at lifePos; alive.collectedGems.clear(); alive.collectedExtraLives.clear();
Related Features: gameBoard.player, gameBoard.getEntityCell, Alive.origPosition, Alive.collectedGems, Alive.collectedExtraLives
Related Classes: GameBoard, MoveResult, Alive, Gem, ExtraLife, Player
Input: prevMove (MoveResult): Previously executed move to undo.
Output: void
Pre-condition: prevMove must be an Alive move. Board state matches post-move state.
Post-condition: Player restored to origPosition. Collected items re-added to board. Board reflects pre-move state.

  public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction)
  {
    Position origPos = gameBoard.getPlayer().getPosition();
    DirectionOffset dirDelta = getDirectionOffset(direction);
    Position curr = origPos;
    int dist = 0;
    BasicEList<Position> collectedGems = new BasicEList<>();
    BasicEList<Position> collectedExtraLives = new BasicEList<>();

    while (true) {
        Position nextPos = curr.offsetByOrNull1(dirDelta.getDRow(), dirDelta.getDCol(), gameBoard.getNumRows(), gameBoard.getNumCols());
        if (nextPos == null || gameBoard.getCell2(nextPos) instanceof Wall) {
            break;
        }
        curr = nextPos;
        dist++;
        Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell2(curr);
        if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
            break;
        }
        if (cell instanceof Mine) {
            return new Dead(origPos, curr);
        }
        if (cell instanceof Gem) {
            collectedGems.add(curr);
            continue;
        }
        if (cell instanceof ExtraLife) {
            collectedExtraLives.add(curr);
            continue;
        }
    }

    if (dist == 0) {
        return new Invalid();
    }

    for (Position pos : collectedGems) {
        gameBoard.removeItemFromBoardAt(pos);
    }
    for (Position pos : collectedExtraLives) {
        gameBoard.removeItemFromBoardAt(pos);
    }
    gameBoard.getPlayer().setOwner(gameBoard.getEntityCell2(curr));
    return new Alive(origPos, curr, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);

  public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction)
  {
    Position origPos = gameBoard.getPlayer().getPosition();
    DirectionOffset dirDelta = getDirectionOffset(direction);
    Position curr = origPos;
    int dist = 0;
    BasicEList<Position> collectedGems = new BasicEList<>();
    BasicEList<Position> collectedExtraLives = new BasicEList<>();

    while (true) {
        Position nextPos = curr.offsetByOrNull1(dirDelta.getDRow(), dirDelta.getDCol(), gameBoard.getNumRows(), gameBoard.getNumCols());
        if (nextPos == null || gameBoard.getCell2(nextPos) instanceof Wall) {
            break;
        }
        curr = nextPos;
        dist++;
        Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell2(curr);
        if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
            break;
        }
        if (cell instanceof Mine) {
            return new Dead(origPos, curr);
        }
        if (cell instanceof Gem) {
            collectedGems.add(curr);
            continue;
        }
        if (cell instanceof ExtraLife) {
            collectedExtraLives.add(curr);
            continue;
        }
    }

    if (dist == 0) {
        return new Invalid();
    }

    for (Position pos : collectedGems) {
        gameBoard.removeItemFromBoardAt(pos);
    }
    for (Position pos : collectedExtraLives) {
        gameBoard.removeItemFromBoardAt(pos);
    }
    gameBoard.getPlayer().setOwner(gameBoard.getEntityCell2(curr));
    return new Alive(origPos, curr, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
  }

  {

    gameBoard.getPlayer().setOwner(gameBoard.getEntityCell2(alive.getOrigPosition()));

        gameBoard.addItemToBoardAt(gemPos, Gem.class);
    }
    for (Position lifePos : alive.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
        gameBoard.addItemToBoardAt(lifePos, ExtraLife.class);
    }
    alive.getCollectedGems().clear();
    alive.getCollectedExtraLives().clear();
  }

    DirectionOffset dirDelta = getDirectionOffset(direction);
    Position curr = origPos;
    int dist = 0;
    BasicEList<Position> collectedGems = new BasicEList<>();
    BasicEList<Position> collectedExtraLives = new BasicEList<>();

    while (true) {
        Position nextPos = curr.offsetByOrNull1(dirDelta.getDRow(), dirDelta.getDCol(), gameBoard.getNumRows(), gameBoard.getNumCols());
        if (nextPos == null || gameBoard.getCell2(nextPos) instanceof Wall) {
            break;
        }
        curr = nextPos;
        dist++;
        Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell2(curr);
        if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
            break;
        }
        if (cell instanceof Mine) {
            return new Dead(origPos, curr);
        }
        if (cell instanceof Gem) {
            collectedGems.add(curr);
            continue;
        }
        if (cell instanceof ExtraLife) {
            collectedExtraLives.add(curr);
            continue;
        }
    }

    if (dist == 0) {
        return new Invalid();
    }

    for (Position pos : collectedGems) {
        gameBoard.removeItemFromBoardAt(pos);
    }
    for (Position pos : collectedExtraLives) {
        gameBoard.removeItemFromBoardAt(pos);
    }
    gameBoard.getPlayer().setOwner(gameBoard.getEntityCell2(curr));
    return new Alive(origPos, curr, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);

    alive.getCollectedExtraLives().clear();

   * Summary: Executes inertial sliding logic for a given direction, determining movement outcome and handling collections/deaths according to grid rules.
   * Algorithm: origPos = gameBoard.player.position; dirDelta = getDirectionOffset(direction); curr = origPos; dist = 0; collectedGems = []; collectedExtraLives = []; while true: nextPos = curr.offsetByOrNull1(dirDelta.dRow, dirDelta.dCol, gameBoard.numRows, gameBoard.numCols); if nextPos == null or gameBoard.getCell2(nextPos) instanceof Wall: break; curr = nextPos; dist++; cell = gameBoard.getCell2(curr); if cell instanceof StopCell: break; if cell instanceof Mine: return new Dead(origPos, curr); if cell instanceof Gem: collectedGems.add(curr); continue; if cell instanceof ExtraLife: collectedExtraLives.add(curr); continue; if dist == 0: return new Invalid(); for pos in collectedGems: removeItemFromBoardAt(pos); for pos in collectedExtraLives: removeItemFromBoardAt(pos); gameBoard.player.setowner(gameBoard.getEntityCell2(curr)); return new Alive(origPos, curr, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
   * Related Features: gameBoard.player, gameBoard.getCell2, gameBoard.getEntityCell2, gameBoard.numRows, gameBoard.numCols, Direction deltas, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Gem, Mine, StopCell, ExtraLife, EntityCell

   * Input: direction (Direction): UP, DOWN, LEFT, or RIGHT.
   * Output: MoveResult: Alive, Dead, or Invalid.
   * Pre-condition: Player is on board. Board configuration and boundaries are complete.
   * Post-condition: Returns appropriate MoveResult. If Alive, player position updates to final cell, collected Gems/ExtraLives are removed from board. If Dead, board and player position remain unchanged. If Invalid, nothing changes.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction)
  {
    Position origPos = gameBoard.getPlayer().getPosition();
    DirectionOffset dirDelta = getDirectionOffset(direction);
    Position curr = origPos;
    int dist = 0;
    BasicEList<Position> collectedGems = new BasicEList<>();
    BasicEList<Position> collectedExtraLives = new BasicEList<>();

    while (true) {
        Position nextPos = curr.offsetByOrNull1(dirDelta.getDRow(), dirDelta.getDCol(), gameBoard.getNumRows(), gameBoard.getNumCols());
        if (nextPos == null || gameBoard.getCell2(nextPos) instanceof Wall) {
            break;
        }
        curr = nextPos;
        dist++;
        Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell2(curr);
        if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
            break;
        }
        if (cell instanceof Mine) {
            return new Dead(origPos, curr);
        }
        if (cell instanceof Gem) {
            collectedGems.add(curr);
            continue;
        }
        if (cell instanceof ExtraLife) {
            collectedExtraLives.add(curr);
            continue;
        }
    }

    if (dist == 0) {
        return new Invalid();
    }

    for (Position pos : collectedGems) {
        gameBoard.removeItemFromBoardAt(pos);
    }
    for (Position pos : collectedExtraLives) {
        gameBoard.removeItemFromBoardAt(pos);
    }
    gameBoard.getPlayer().setOwner(gameBoard.getEntityCell2(curr));
    return new Alive(origPos, curr, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->

   * Algorithm: if prevMove not instanceof Alive: throw IllegalArgumentException("Cannot undo non-Alive move"); alive = (Alive) prevMove; gameBoard.player.setowner(gameBoard.getEntityCell2(alive.origPosition)); for gemPos in alive.collectedGems: addItemToBoardAt(gemPos, Gem); for lifePos in alive.collectedExtraLives: addItemToBoardAt(lifePos, ExtraLife); alive.collectedGems.clear(); alive.collectedExtraLives.clear(); // Note: Finite ExtraLife gain reversal is handled by GameState.processUndo per requirements

   * Post-condition: Player restored to origPosition. Collected items re-added to board. Alive collected lists cleared. Board reflects pre-move state.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove)
  {
    if (!(prevMove instanceof Alive)) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cannot undo non-Alive move");
    }
    Alive alive = (Alive) prevMove;
    gameBoard.getPlayer().setOwner(gameBoard.getEntityCell2(alive.getOrigPosition()));
    for (Position gemPos : alive.getCollectedGems()) {
        gameBoard.addItemToBoardAt(gemPos, Gem.class);
    }
    for (Position lifePos : alive.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
        gameBoard.addItemToBoardAt(lifePos, ExtraLife.class);
    }
    alive.getCollectedGems().clear();
    alive.getCollectedExtraLives().clear();
  }
